 WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal crackdown on alleged food stamp fraud is putting the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, known as SNAP, back in the political spotlight, as the Trump Administration argues the safety-net program has become “rife with fraud” and Democrats warn the administration has weakened oversight while tightening eligibility.
 The Justice Department says $42 million has been stolen from the program, sometimes by thieves operating from other countries. (TNND) 
 “For more than 50 years,” SNAP has served as a lifeline for working families in need and retirees, providing funds to buy groceries and put food on the table. But Attorney General Todd Blanche said the administration views the fraud issue as part of a broader fight over the program’s future.
 “This is literally a concerted effort to take food out of the mouths of children,” Blanche said.
 The administration has pointed to cases it says show widespread abuse, including the indictment earlier this month of social media i nfluencer Shawty Dred on charges that include food stamp fraud and aggravated identity theft. In a statement about the case, Vice President JD Vance said, “The simple fact is, this is a man that we have connected to $4.4 million in fraud against the Snap program. Snap exists to help hungry children eat. It does not exist to provide private jets to a guy like Shawty Dred.”
 The Justice Department says $42 million has been stolen from the program, sometimes by thieves operating from other countries. One defendant, Fernandez Guzman from the Dominican Republic, is charged with stealing the identity of a U.S. citizen to obtain multiple driver’s licenses, as well as $22,000 in SNAP benefits.
 The announcement of the latest enforcement actions came a day after President Donald Trump unveiled a $25 million rewards program for Americans who report fraud. “It will save trillions, I believe trillions,” Trump said.
 But while the administration has made cracking down on fraud a top priority, it also cut millions of dollars and hundreds of staff members who helped address fraud, including multiple inspectors general.
 During a June 25 hearing looking at SNAP fraud, 
 Rep. James Walkinshaw, D-Va., said, “SNAP fraud is a real issue. And thats why we need qualified independent non-partisan non-political IGs. The Trump administration has systematically fired them.”
 Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill,” backed by President Trump, also resulted in more than five million people losing SNAP benefits, with new restrictions, added work requirements and more costs to the states.
